# Hopf Frame Compilation

> Exact and Fault-Tolerant Compilation of Hopf Differential Frames, by Ruge Lin. A theoretical quantum-circuit compilation repository with proofs and executable finite checks for prescribed complete Hopf frames, clean and borrowed workspace, and Clifford+T resource bounds.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation

## When to consult this repository

- Prescribed unitary completions: the state column and designated differential-frame columns used by Hopf quantum backpropagation (QBP).
- Exact circuit size, CNOT count, and ancilla-depth tradeoffs for complete Hopf frames.
- Fault-tolerant Clifford+T synthesis: T-count and T-depth versus precision, clean ancillas, and dirty or borrowed qubits entangled with external references.
- One-clean-qubit compilation, conditional logical-suffix workspace, literal diagonals, and complete one-target U(2) multiplexors.
- Fixed-parameter gradient robustness and a separate state-based QBP decoder that avoids fine complete-frame synthesis.

Start with the current theorem and its assumptions, not a historical intermediate bound. Upper constructions apply to every admitted parameter tuple; matching lower bounds are worst-case statements over the specified family. Record the exact commit consulted and use CITATION.cff for attribution.

The bounded internal audit of Results A–D is complete without an unresolved claim-level blocker. The selected scientific scope is frozen, final manuscript writing remains on hold, and the two open resource gaps are optional research. See docs/CORE_CLAIM_AUDIT.md and WORKSPACE.md for the reviewed dependencies, evidence limits, and reopening gate. This is not independent peer review or formal proof certification.

## Current complete-frame results

Write N=2^n, n>=1, 0<eta<=1/64, L=max{6,ceil(log2(1/eta))}, B0=L+n+7, h=1+ceil(log2(L+n+2)), and ell_*(n)=1+log2^*(n+2). The iterated logarithm counts repeated base-two logarithms until the value is at most one. In Clifford+T bounds, a and b count initialized clean and arbitrary dirty compiler qubits, and q_tot=n+a+b. G counts elementary Clifford gates.

### Exact compilation

With arbitrary one-qubit gates, CNOTs, all-to-all connectivity, and any integer m>=0 clean work qubits, the prescribed real and phase-dressed complex magnitude frames have:

- Total elementary size Theta(N).
- CNOT count Theta(N) for n>=2; zero CNOTs for n=1.
- Elementary depth Theta(n+N/(n+m)).

Workspace returns exactly. These are matching orders, not optimal leading constants. See docs/COMPILER_THEOREM.md.

### Precision and workspace in T-count

The sufficient-clean theorem gives T*=Theta(sqrt(NL)+L+NL/q_tot), with G=O(NL), for both real and phase-dressed complex magnitude frames when a>=C(n+h) for a sufficiently large fixed C. This clean reservation is sufficient; it is not asserted necessary. See docs/FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPILER.md.

The one-clean grouped real-frame compiler gives T=O(N+L ell_*(n)), G=O(NL), at a=1 and b>=B0. With b>=2B0, its banked refinement gives T=O(sqrt(NL)+L ell_*(n)+NL/b). Under that reservation it matches the lower bound when L ell_*(n)^2<=N or b<=N/ell_*(n). See docs/ONE_CLEAN_COMPILER.md and docs/CONDITIONAL_SUFFIX_COMPILER.md.

A separate literal diagonal composes with the real frame to compile D_phi W_real for supplied certified leaf phases. This phase-dressed complex magnitude extension uses b>=L+n+8 for the unbanked one-clean bound, or b>=2(L+n+8) for the banked bound. It does not compile arbitrary complex unitaries; phase derivatives use a separate measurement stream.

Other allocations retain distinct constructions. For every a,b>=0 the real-frame borrowed-workspace bound is T=O(NL/q_tot+L sqrt(N)), G=O(NL); its matching splice has the additional condition h+b<=c sqrt(N) for fixed c>0. A zero-clean real-frame construction gives T=O(N+nL), G=O(NL), at b>=B0. Neither statement removes the grouped compiler's clean predicate or the literal-phase primitive's initialized flag. Literal diagonals and complete U(2) multiplexors have separately matched one-stage bounds and their own dirty reservations in docs/ONE_CLEAN_COMPILER.md.

### Simultaneous real-frame T-count and T-depth

The uniform theorem uses a=2 and the literal reservation b>=17B0. One complete real-frame circuit has absolute-constant bounds:

T=O(sqrt(NL)+NL/b+nL), G=O(NL), D_T=O(NL/b^2+nL).

For 6<=L<=log2(n+2)/16, the same theorem strengthens these to:

T=O(sqrt(NL)+NL/b), G=O(NL), D_T=O(NL/b^2+n).

Always subject to b>=17B0, and only when the intervals are nonempty:

- Every precision: b<=sqrt(N/n) gives T*=Theta(NL/b) and D_T*=Theta(NL/b^2).
- The displayed slowly growing precision range: the same matching orders hold through b<=sqrt(NL/n).

Outside these intervals the general count retains nL. The sufficient condition L<=N/n^2 absorbs nL into sqrt(NL), giving optimal-order count at every eligible width. The small coefficient in the slowly growing precision range is an asymptotic sufficient condition, not a practical crossover estimate. See docs/UNIFORM_PRECISION_DEPTH.md.

At fixed eta, the blocked-bilinear theorem gives T=O_eta(sqrt(N)+N/b), G=O_eta(N), and D_T=O_eta(N/b^2+n), under the same b>=17B0 reservation. At sufficient b=Theta_eta(sqrt(N)), this is optimal-order T=Theta_eta(sqrt(N)) together with D_T=O_eta(n). The unrestricted depth lower bound there remains Omega(1). Constants in this fixed-eta statement may depend on eta; the uniform theorem's constants do not. Earlier schedules remain fallbacks at their smaller literal reservations. See docs/BLOCKED_BILINEAR_LOOKUP.md and docs/UNARY_PHASE_GRADIENT.md.

These depth theorems are for real complete frames. They are not automatically complex-frame or state-based QBP theorems. T-depth counts T/T-dagger layers separated by arbitrary Clifford circuits; it is not elementary circuit depth or elapsed execution time.

## Separate completed state-based QBP contract

The state-based theorem changes the measurement decoder. It covers all-angle real Hopf states and both magnitude and phase gradients of phase-dressed complex states, including singular coordinates. It prescribes initialized state preparation rather than every column of the fine unitary. The complex protocol uses its declared phase gauge.

Keep requested gradient precision K separate from the state precision floor P=max{n,K}; the theorem chooses K from the desired absolute gradient accuracy and observable coefficient scale. Two initialized compiler flags and b>=P+n+7 dirty wires give T=O(N+P), G=O(NP) per execution, apart from observable access. The initialized system, protocol interference branch, and observable work are additional reservations. Observable precision remains K even when P=n>K.

The construction charges a native coarse reference, its actual inverse, coherent reference/target preparation, both original raw-gradient streams, and classical reconstruction. Its initialized-isometry error includes dirty/reference return and work leakage. All sampling executions, observable access, coefficient preprocessing, and output costs remain separately charged. Banked count and real/complex depth schedules have their own sufficient reservations; use docs/STATE_BASED_QBP_THEOREM.md and docs/STATE_QBP_DEPTH.md for the complete statements.

The analytic theorem and bounded native integrations are complete. A general elementary emitter, a general software interface, and an application-level advantage are not selected prerequisites. State preparation does not close either complete-frame gap below. The cost comparison retains classical baselines and does not prove optimal gradient estimation or an end-to-end speedup.

## Research decision and two optional open gaps

1. Fixed-accuracy, large-width complete-frame T-depth: at a=2 and sufficient b=Theta_eta(sqrt(N)), the current bounds are Omega(1)<=D_T*<=O_eta(n), with optimal-order T-count in the upper construction.
2. Constant-clean, high-precision complete-frame count: at a=2, L=N, b=N+n+7, and n>=3, Omega(N)<=T*<=O(N ell_*(n)). The one-clean construction attains the same upper bound. The uniform-depth width threshold excludes this literal endpoint, and its unary-source mechanism does not scale to this precision.

These gaps are optional extensions of the established package. No new construction pass is active without a qualifying native rule. Follow [WORKSPACE.md#research-decision-and-stopping-rules](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/blob/main/WORKSPACE.md#research-decision-and-stopping-rules).

The current large-width depth ledger still has two independent O(n) allowances: logical transport and program load/unload. Protected-source boundaries, windowed activity predicates, and late work have smaller allowances. A logarithmic-depth stabilizer-completion component does not remove the sequential transport or the query cost. Improving one component alone does not establish a sublinear complete-frame theorem.

Reopen a construction route only with an explicit composition rule, symbolic depth/count/width recurrence, and full cleanup contract. An exact retained-source rewrite must hold on every source input; an ideal-source-only alternative needs a global initialized-isometry proof. A proposed lower bound must survive the admitted arbitrary Clifford interlayers and returned dirty work. More fixed-size matrices, phase rearrangements, stale-cache variants, or interface-specific obstructions do not by themselves justify another research pass. See docs/OPEN_PROBLEM.md for completed attempts and their precise boundaries.

## Contracts and evidence boundaries

- No QRAM, intermediate measurement/reset, postselection, supplied catalyst, free precision source, uncharged initialized history, target-frame oracle, or free coherent evaluator is assumed.
- The complete-frame error is an operator-norm initialized-isometry bound: ||V J_a-J_a(W tensor I_dirty)||<=eta. It includes every logical input, arbitrary dirty inputs and external references, literal phases, and clean-work leakage.
- Return promises depend on the construction. Exact compilation returns all work exactly; the sufficient-clean compiler returns dirty work exactly. One-clean and original two-clean operator cores return approximately within the stated norm while lookup/control work returns exactly. Conditional logical-suffix work is clean only on its active sector; inactive behavior and final return must be proved separately.
- Supplied angles/phases admit certified evaluation. Classical coefficient generation and table preprocessing are outside quantum gate counts; the bounded-input QBP audit states when classical construction is efficient.
- Finite native checks and exact certificates support specified identities and ledgers. They do not prove asymptotic bounds, establish priority, or supply independent peer review. No general elementary Clifford+T emitter for the full asymptotic compiler is claimed.

- [Core-claim audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/CORE_CLAIM_AUDIT.md): Completed internal claim-to-proof review of Results A–D, source premises, correction, and scope-freeze decision.
- [Frame-safe compilation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/FRAME_SAFE_COMPILATION.md): Operational necessity of the complete frame and singular exceptions.
- [Exact compilation theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/COMPILER_THEOREM.md): Matching exact size, CNOT count, and clean-workspace depth.
- [Fault-tolerant frame theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPILER.md): Sufficient-clean matching T-count and phase-dressed complex extension.
- [One-clean compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/ONE_CLEAN_COMPILER.md): One-clean frame, diagonal, and multiplexor bounds; complex and borrowed-signal corollaries with distinct reservations.
- [Conditional-suffix compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/CONDITIONAL_SUFFIX_COMPILER.md): Grouped precision sharing, banked refinement, inactive identity, and complete return error.
- [Borrowed-workspace compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/BORROWED_WORKSPACE_COMPILER.md): Arbitrary allocations and its restricted matching splice.
- [Uniform count and depth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/UNIFORM_PRECISION_DEPTH.md): Strongest uniform real-frame composition and simultaneous matching intervals.
- [Blocked bilinear lookup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/BLOCKED_BILINEAR_LOOKUP.md): Fixed-accuracy variable-width count/depth theorem.
- [Unary phase source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/UNARY_PHASE_GRADIENT.md): Charged selected shifts, complete-frame O_eta(n) depth, exact retained-source factors, and shallow stabilizer completion with sequential transport still charged.
- [State-based QBP theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/STATE_BASED_QBP_THEOREM.md): Separate completed real/complex state contract, accuracy, workspace, sampling, and bounded implementation.
- [State-based QBP depth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/STATE_QBP_DEPTH.md): Separate same-circuit depth/count schedules and dirty reservations.
- [QBP approximation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/QBP_APPROXIMATION.md): Original frame-based robustness, complex gradients, observables, and dirty-bank reuse.
- [Complete task-cost comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/QBP_COST_COMPARISON.md): Common accuracy/workspace, all quantum executions, observable access, preprocessing, reconstruction, and classical baselines.
- [Research status](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/OPEN_PROBLEM.md): The two open complete-frame frontiers, completed component work, and scoped failure diagnostics.
- [Documentation map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/README.md): Full proof and supporting-material index.
